bugs.summary: sprintf() with a width or precision near INT_MAX overflows the C stack (glibc 2.31) or silently returns ""
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
sprintf() passes a field width or precision near .Machine$integer.max
straight to the C library. On glibc 2.31 (e.g. Ubuntu 20.04) that
overflows the C stack in a standard x86_64 R build; where it doesn't
crash, sprintf() silently returns "" instead of a result or an error.

Reproducible example:

    sprintf("%2147483647s", "a")
    sprintf("%.2147483647s", "a")
    sprintf("%*s", .Machine$integer.max, "a")

Observed:

  - x86_64 Ubuntu 20.04 (glibc 2.31), with the distribution's R 3.6.3:
    the first two give "Error: segfault from C stack overflow". R-devel
    r90601 on glibc 2.31 fails the same way on all three whenever printf
    hooks are registered (see below; tested on aarch64, which has no
    libquadmath, with a small LD_PRELOAD library registering a hook in
    its place).
  - glibc 2.31 without printf hooks: all three return "".
  - macOS (R-devel r90464): the first and third return "".

Expected: the first and third signal the error sprintf() already gives
for any width above 8192,

    Error in sprintf("%2147483647s", "a") :
      required resulting string length 2147483647 is greater than maximal 8192

and the second returns "a".

Analysis: do_sprintf() in src/main/sprintf.c (trunk r90601) hands each
conversion specification to snprintf() unchanged and only checks
afterwards that the result fits in MAXLINE (8192) bytes. glibc 2.31
rejects widths and precisions from INT_MAX - 32 up with EOVERFLOW on its
fast path. But once any printf hooks are registered
(register_printf_specifier() and friends), it formats every call through
printf_positional(), where MAX (prec, width) + EXTSIZ (EXTSIZ is 32)
overflows int while sizing the work buffer, and the alloca() that
follows runs off the end of the stack (stdio-common/vfprintf-internal.c,
line 2016 in 2.31). libquadmath registers such hooks when it is loaded,
and x86_64 Linux builds of R load it through libgfortran, so an ordinary
R session is affected. That alloca() is gone by glibc 2.35, and the
glibc 2.28 in Rocky 8 does not crash. Where the libc returns -1 instead
(glibc 2.31 without hooks for widths and precisions, macOS for widths),
the nc > MAXLINE check lets it through and sprintf() returns whatever
its buffer holds.

This was found by OSS-Fuzz, with AddressSanitizer, on the sprintf target
in https://github.com/r-devel/r-oss-fuzz, from the input
sprintf("%2147483647s", "fuzz"):

    ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-overflow
        #0 printf_positional     stdio-common/vfprintf-internal.c:2016
        #1 __vfprintf_internal   stdio-common/vfprintf-internal.c:1733
        #2 __vsnprintf_internal  libio/vsnprintf.c:114
        #5 do_sprintf            src/main/sprintf.c:435

Proposed patch: attached as sprintf-huge-width.diff (against r90601). A
new boundspec() checks the format just before each snprintf() call in
do_sprintf(). A width above MAXLINE signals the existing "required
resulting string length" error before the call instead of after it. A
precision above MAXLINE is lowered to MAXLINE + 1, which cannot change a
result that fits: where precision sets a minimum length (%d, %f, %e,
%#g) the result is still too long, and for %s and %g it already exceeds
any string that fits and any significant digit of a double. The check
runs after checkfmt(), so invalid formats keep their existing errors,
and '*' arguments are covered because they have already been expanded
by then.

Results for 42 other formats (ordinary ones, '*' arguments, NA/Inf,
widths at and just over the limit, and large precisions such as
"%.100000g" and "%.9000s") are identical with the patch, on glibc 2.31
and on macOS, except for the length quoted in the error for formats
that fail either way: sprintf("%.9000f", 1) now reports 8195 rather
than 9002. make test-Reg passes.

Bug 19188 reports a crash from the same kind of input in format() and
formatC(); that is a separate int overflow in do_format() (paste.c),
which this patch does not touch.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/346,
where CI results can be seen.

comments.creator: luke
comments.text: This feels like it might be something that should be rported and handled upstream by glibc?

Created attachment 3879
patch v2: bound sprintf() width and precision, with regression tests

Good point -- and it turns out it has been: this is glibc bug 26211,
"printf integer overflow calculating allocation size"
(https://sourceware.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=26211), fixed in glibc
2.32 by removing that allocation from printf_positional(). (I wrote 2.35
above; 2.32 is the first release without it.) Ubuntu 20.04's glibc 2.31
doesn't carry the fix, which is why R there, and the OSS-Fuzz runner,
still crash. The glibc 2.28 in Rocky 8 doesn't crash, presumably through
a backport.

So the crash itself is glibc's, and it's fixed there. I'd still suggest
the R-side change, for reasons that don't depend on that bug:

  - snprintf() may fail with EOVERFLOW when the output would not fit in
    an int, and libcs refuse widths near INT_MAX that way: macOS returns
    -1 for "%2147483647s", and so does glibc 2.31's non-positional path.
    sprintf() only checks nc > MAXLINE, so the -1 goes through and it
    silently returns "", on macOS today and on glibc 2.31 without printf
    hooks.
  - A width above MAXLINE can only end in the length error anyway, so
    checking it before the call costs nothing and gives the same result
    on every platform, including older glibc that is still in use.

If you'd rather keep the change smaller, treating nc < 0 as an error in
_my_sprintf would fix the silent "" everywhere, though not the crash on
glibc 2.31 with printf hooks.

I've also attached sprintf-huge-width-v2.diff, which replaces attachment
3878. The change to src/main/sprintf.c is identical; v2 adds regression
tests at the end of tests/reg-tests-1e.R. They assert the usual length
error for widths given in the format, through '*', and beyond INT_MAX,
and that huge precisions give the right result ("a" for
"%.2147483647s", and the same string as "%.9000g" for "%.2147483647g").
Without the fix, the width checks fail on macOS, all of them fail on
glibc 2.31 without printf hooks, and glibc 2.31 with hooks crashes. With
it, reg-tests-1e.R and make test-Reg pass.

Patch also at https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/346
